items.headline: Singapore brings forward S$500 CDC vouchers to June 11 as Gulf conflict lifts costs
items.summary: Eligible Singaporean households can claim a S$500 CDC voucher tranche from June 11, brought forward from January 2027 in response to higher fuel prices and cost-of-living anxieties from the Middle East conflict; the payout is split S$250 for hawkers and heartland merchants and S$250 for supermarkets.

items.headline: Workers told to reapply for overseas roles are still retrenched, MOM and NTUC say
items.summary: The Ministry of Manpower and NTUC said employees who lose their jobs in Singapore count as retrenched even when asked to reapply for roles overseas within the same firm, as union-handled cases climb and total layoffs rose to 14,490 in 2025 from 13,020 in 2024.

items.headline: Singapore police warn of resurgent concert-ticket and impersonation scams
items.summary: Singapore police renewed warnings over concert-ticket resale scams and government-official impersonation calls, after the ICA flagged scammers posing as officers on phone and video calls to extract payments and personal data.

items.headline: Singapore Airlines keeps Dubai route suspended as Gulf airspace stays volatile
items.summary: Renewed US-Iran strikes this week kept Gulf airspace disrupted, with Singapore Airlines holding its Singapore-Dubai service (SQ494/SQ495) suspended through August 2, deferring its Riyadh launch to September and keeping Scoot's Jeddah flights halted.

items.headline: Three Indian seafarers killed in US strike on tanker off Oman; New Delhi summons US envoy
items.summary: India's foreign ministry confirmed three Indian crew were killed when a US aircraft struck the oil tanker MT Settebello in the Gulf of Oman, which Washington said it disabled for trying to smuggle Iranian oil past its blockade; the Indian Navy rescued 21 other Indian nationals and New Delhi summoned a senior US diplomat.

items.headline: Naga body enforces 24-hour Manipur shutdown after six abducted villagers found dead
items.summary: The United Naga Council enforced a 24-hour shutdown across Naga-inhabited areas of Manipur from 6am on June 11 after the bodies of six Naga villagers, abducted on May 13 from Leilon Vaiphei, were recovered in Kangpokpi district; the council demanded arrests and the scrapping of the Suspension of Operations pact with Kuki militant groups.

items.headline: India's forex reserves rise to $682.32 billion in latest RBI data
items.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves climbed to $682.32 billion in the latest weekly Reserve Bank of India data, extending a recovery even as the rupee stays under pressure from higher oil prices linked to the Gulf conflict.

items.headline: West Bengal becomes 36th state to roll out Ayushman Bharat health scheme
items.summary: West Bengal began implementing the Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY health insurance scheme on June 8, becoming the 36th state or union territory to do so and extending cover of up to 5 lakh rupees a family to its residents.

items.headline: Update: Trump calls off Iran strikes, says ceasefire-and-Hormuz deal is close
items.summary: President Trump said on June 11 he had cancelled planned strikes on Iran, hours after threatening to hit it very hard, and claimed a deal to extend the ceasefire, reopen the Strait of Hormuz and start 60 days of nuclear talks was nearly done; Iran's foreign ministry said no final agreement had been reached.

items.headline: Update: Northern Ireland sees second night of unrest after Belfast stabbing
items.summary: Rioters in Northern Ireland set fires and threw bricks and bottles at police for a second night on June 10 over an attempted-murder stabbing in Belfast, as anti-immigration violence spread and political leaders again appealed for calm.

items.headline: Saudi Arabia lifts five-year ban on Lebanese imports in sign of thaw
items.summary: Saudi Arabia lifted a near-five-year ban on Lebanese imports on June 10, an order from Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman that Riyadh tied to positive steps by Beirut, including moves to disarm Hezbollah; Lebanese President Joseph Aoun said it would help revive the economy.

items.headline: China bars Philippine defence chief Teodoro over South China Sea remarks
items.summary: China's foreign ministry said on June 11 it was banning Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro and his family from entering China, Hong Kong and Macau, and barring transactions with him, over his erroneous remarks on the South China Sea; Manila called it an unfriendly act.

items.headline: Largest-ever World Cup opens as hosts Mexico beat South Africa 2-0
items.summary: The 48-team, 104-match FIFA World Cup co-hosted by the US, Mexico and Canada opened on June 11 with hosts Mexico beating South Africa 2-0 before a packed Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.

items.headline: EU orders Meta to open WhatsApp to rival AI assistants
items.summary: The European Commission ordered Meta to let third-party AI chatbots operate inside WhatsApp, saying users must be free to choose their AI assistant, in a fresh Digital Markets Act intervention against the messaging service.

items.headline: OpenAI teams with Oracle to sell its models and Codex through OCI
items.summary: OpenAI said Oracle Cloud customers will soon be able to apply their existing Oracle credits to buy OpenAI frontier models, including GPT-5.5, and its Codex coding tool through the OCI Marketplace.

items.headline: Qualcomm strikes ByteDance deal to supply AI data-centre chips
items.summary: Qualcomm agreed to supply ByteDance with millions of custom ASIC chips for AI data centres powering agents in its Doubao chatbot, pushing the company deeper into the data-centre silicon market.

items.headline: OpenAI says Chinese operations used ChatGPT for covert influence content
items.summary: OpenAI reported that China-linked operations had used ChatGPT to generate political content, including cartoons aimed at US policy debates, as part of covert influence campaigns it said it had detected and disrupted.

items.headline: Update: Wall Street surges as Trump cancels Iran strikes
items.summary: US stocks jumped on June 11 after President Trump called off planned strikes on Iran and signalled a deal: the S&P 500 rose 1.75% to 7,394.30, the Dow climbed 929.97 points (1.86%) to 50,848.75 and the Nasdaq gained 2.54% to 25,809.66, led by a rebound in chip stocks.

items.headline: Oracle shares slide about 8% on plan to raise $20 billion for AI build-out
items.summary: Oracle shares fell roughly 8% on June 11 after the company unveiled plans to raise about $20 billion in debt and equity to fund its AI data-centre expansion, with capital-spending guidance above Wall Street estimates overshadowing an earnings beat.

items.headline: Update: Oil tumbles as Trump cancels Iran strikes and touts Hormuz deal
items.summary: Crude prices fell sharply on June 11 after Trump called off strikes on Iran and said the Strait of Hormuz would reopen under a pending deal, unwinding part of the war-risk premium that had driven Brent toward the mid-$90s.

items.headline: US wholesale prices post biggest annual jump in over three years
items.summary: US producer prices rose more than expected in May for the largest annual increase in over three years, reinforcing bets the Federal Reserve will hold rates at its June 17 meeting even as equities rallied.

items.headline: Bangladesh beat Australia to clinch their first ODI series win over Australia
items.summary: Bangladesh beat Australia by five wickets in the second ODI at Mirpur on June 11, chasing a rain-revised target to take an unbeatable lead and seal their first-ever bilateral ODI series win over Australia.

items.headline: Iva Jovic upsets Eala to reach her first Queen's quarter-final
items.summary: Sixth seed Iva Jovic beat Alexandra Eala 6-2, 6-2 at Queen's on June 11 to reach the quarter-finals of the grass-court WTA 500 event for the first time.

items.headline: Pliskova reaches Queen's quarter-finals after Mboko retires
items.summary: Karolina Pliskova advanced to the Queen's quarter-finals on June 11 when Victoria Mboko retired hurt while serving at 4-3 down in the second set, having lost the first set 6-2.

items.headline: Anisimova advances to the Queen's quarter-finals
items.summary: Amanda Anisimova came through her round-of-16 match against Laura Siegemund to reach the quarter-finals of the grass-court event at Queen's.

fun_fact.headline: There are more possible games of chess than atoms in the observable universe
fun_fact.body: There are more possible games of chess than there are atoms in the observable universe. Claude Shannon estimated the number of possible chess games at around 10^120, a figure now called the Shannon number, while the observable universe is thought to hold only about 10^80 atoms, leaving chess's possibilities greater by some 40 orders of magnitude.
fun_fact.source: Claude Shannon, Programming a Computer for Playing Chess (1950); Encyclopaedia Britannica

puzzle.title: The Paper and the Punch
puzzle.body: You take a square sheet of paper and fold it exactly in half from top to bottom, then fold it in half again from left to right, leaving a smaller square that is four sheets thick. You punch one single round hole straight through the middle of this folded square, then carefully unfold the paper completely. How many holes are in the sheet, and how are they arranged?
puzzle.approach: Picture how many layers your single punch actually goes through, then mentally unfold the sheet one crease at a time.
puzzle.answer: Four holes. Folding twice stacks the paper into four layers, so the single punch passes through all four at once. When unfolded, the punched point is mirrored across both crease lines, so the holes land at the centres of the four quadrants, forming a neat 2x2 grid evenly spaced around the middle of the sheet.
